requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: node1 (OPNsense) was configured with opt1 (vtnet1, 10.10.10.1/24, LAN_A) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.10.20.1/24, LAN_B), interfaces were brought up via configctl reconfigure, and node2/node3 were given static IPs and cross routes via node1. Bidirectional ping between 10.10.10.2 (node2) and 10.10.20.2 (node3) through node1 succeeded, directly demonstrating routing.

requirements.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: Block rules for tcp/23 in both directions between opt1/opt2 were added and confirmed present in the loaded pf ruleset (with quick+log), while a general pass rule preserves other traffic. A live TCP/23 connection attempt from node2 to a listener on node3 timed out, directly confirming the block is enforced while ICMP/other traffic passes.

requirements.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
requirements.summary: The block rules were configured with logging enabled, and node1's /var/log/filter/filter_*.log directly shows block entries tied to the telnet-block rule labels (b5fbe32d... and f34060...) with tcp/23 traffic between the lan-a and lan-b subnets, confirming refused attempts are logged.

requirements.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
requirements.summary: node2 (10.10.10.2) initiated a TCP/23 connection to node3 (10.10.20.2) which timed out (refused). The corresponding filter log on node1 shows sequenceIds 209-211 with matching source/destination/port (10.10.10.2 -> 10.10.20.2:23) tied directly to that attempt, and a repeat post-restart attempt (sequenceIds 147-149) confirms the same behavior.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (OPNsense)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot time (16:24:13) and healthy interface/firewall state were captured, a reboot was issued, SSH connection timeouts confirmed the disruption, a new boot time (16:29:05) confirmed the restart, and post-restart interfaces, firewall rules, and the block+log telnet behavior (fresh logged refusal from node2) were all directly re-verified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2 (AlmaLinux)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (d6298ced...) and healthy static IP/route were captured, systemctl reboot was issued, a connection timeout confirmed disruption, a new boot_id (086ac571...) confirmed restart, and post-restart IP, route, and ping connectivity to node1 were directly re-verified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node3 (AlmaLinux)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (5fb1b173...) and healthy static IP/route were captured, systemctl reboot was issued, a connection timeout confirmed disruption, a new boot_id (8e43826c...) confirmed restart, and post-restart IP, route, and ping connectivity to node1 were directly re-verified.

overall_summary: All four material task outcomes are directly satisfied: node1 routes lan-a/lan-b, TCP/23 is blocked between them, refused attempts are logged on node1, and a specific log entry produced by a node2-initiated attempt is shown (both pre- and post-restart). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated on all three nodes (pre-restart baseline, disruption, boot-identity change, and recovered network/firewall/logging state). Hygiene is good overall, with only minor leftover test-listener artifact files on node3.
limitations: Filter log evidence is truncated/tail-based; only a bounded window of log lines was captured rather than the full log file, though the matching entries for the node2 attempts are directly present.
Minor temp-file residue (telnetd*.log/pid) from the TCP/23 test listener remains on node3 after cleanup of the listener process itself.

node1's /tmp/tmpcfd_* churn between before/after snapshots appears to be normal OPNsense config-compile temp file rotation rather than executor-introduced residue, but this could not be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were largely necessary and well-scoped: interface/route configuration on all three nodes, firewall rule additions, and restart-verification commands all had clear roles. One failed mutation attempt (cmd-74726d34b24e4dd2, 'configctl interface reload' returned 'Action not allowed or missing') left no observable state change and was immediately corrected with the working invoke/reconfigure sequence. The main hygiene issue is minor residue from test tooling: a Python TCP/23 listener was started twice on node3 for verification (cmd-1d7761f4c4d34801, cmd-c8145bbc482948e6) and stopped both times (cmd-589da0e685e44f34, cmd-2fbb12c08d834cdc), but the associated /tmp/telnetd.log, /tmp/telnetd.pid, /tmp/telnetd2.log, /tmp/telnetd2.pid files were left behind on node3 per the after_executor snapshot. This is bounded, low-risk, non-destructive residue directly tied to legitimate verification of the block rule, not an unrelated experiment.
